analysis:
The supplied units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md, lines 1212-2036. The patch for this file changes only the 'Last updated' date (line 3), the Nemotron Super inline-media body cap wording (lines ~128-132) and a matching later paragraph (~542-544). Everything else in the supplied units is unchanged context. The changed ranges fall outside the two supplied line windows, so I could not see the changed lines directly. The patch excerpt shows the documented NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes moving from 8 MiB to 40 MiB, the error being renamed to media_too_large, and the failure staying a 400 client error. It also keeps the media-memory 503 when the shared budget cannot hold the charge. The doc says the new cap is sized for one part at the shared 25 MiB inline-media cap as base64. This is a documentation change only, with no code in the supplied evidence.

If the underlying code change matches, a larger encoded-body cap could raise memory and DoS exposure for TB-007 and TB-002 (T-010 and T-029 are adjacent). The doc says the reservation is still taken from the shared budget before decoding and refused with 503 if it does not fit. Whether that reservation precedes the body buffering, and what the transport-level body limits are, lies outside the supplied evidence. The Swift implementation and coordinator transport limits should be checked in whichever batch carries the code.

The supplied unchanged sections (prefill geometry, deadlines, MTP, sampling, prefix cache references) do not touch the T-041 mitigations. The SSD cache TTL, HMAC naming and cache salt are unchanged. No new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumptions were identified from the documentation itself.
